SMTO-HTTP-0051 — The Gateway couldn't handle this web request

GUID: 3e1300e0-9698-4dd9-960f-7b5ab8b82410
Slug: http-gateway-error
Domain: HTTP · Subsystem: http

What happened

  • The Gateway, the helper program SMTO uses to reach other services from a computer, rejected or failed this web request, so SMTO didn't get a usable answer back.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Settings › Setup › Gateways and check that the Gateway used for this task shows Connected rather than Connection failed. This error comes from the Gateway itself, so it must be running and connected before anything else will help.
  2. On the same screen, select Check for updates and install any update offered for that Gateway. A Gateway on a different version from SMTO can refuse web requests it doesn't understand.
  3. If the step was changing something on another service, open that service and check whether the change already happened before asking the Agent to try again. SMTO didn't get a clear answer, so repeating a change without checking could do it twice.

What success looks like

  • The Gateway shows Connected and the Agent's next web request returns a result instead of this error.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the Gateway's name, to the person who manages that Gateway. Don't delete the Gateway or remove its pairing to clear this; that throws away its trusted setup and settings.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The outbound Gateway's /http/request handler raised an HTTP error (HTTPException) while dispatching the native HTTP request, so the Server received a generic Gateway failure instead of an HTTP receipt.

What this means

  • The outbound Gateway wrapper converted an HTTPException from native HTTP dispatch into a Gateway runtime failure response. The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.

Why this can happen

  • The outbound Gateway wrapper converted an HTTPException from native HTTP dispatch into a Gateway runtime failure response.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the Gateway route exception/status and initialization evidence; this code does not by itself prove missing dependencies.

How to fix it

  • Check the Gateway's log on its host for the /http/request failure, its status and any X-SMTO-Rejection reason. Confirm the Gateway build matches the Server (Settings › Setup › Gateways › Check for updates), update or repair it in place, let it reconnect, and inspect the target's state before repeating any write.
  • Inspect the Gateway native HTTP support and installed dependencies. Update or repair the matching Gateway build and reconnect before another request.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The selected Gateway's native HTTP route returns a valid supported response.

What not to do

  • Do not remove retained state or weaken trust checks to make an unavailable dependency appear healthy.

Technical notes

  • The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
